- Policy stance: The FOMC held the target range at 5.25–5.50% and continues QT, emphasizing “some further progress” toward 2% and a better balance of risks, but wants greater confidence before cutting.
- Beige Book overlay (latest report across Districts): Overall activity was slight-to-modest, not “solid.” Consumer spending was mixed, manufacturing was flat-to-softer, and CRE—especially office—remained weak. Labor demand eased further with improved worker availability; wage growth moderated. Price increases slowed somewhat, with more reports of reduced cost pressures. Loan demand softened and credit standards remained tight; delinquencies edged up from low levels.
- SLOOS overlay (July): Banks continued to tighten across C&I, CRE, residential mortgages/HELOCs, and consumer credit; demand weakened broadly, and spreads remained elevated.
- Implications: Beige Book and SLOOS both temper the growth narrative implied by “solid pace,” reinforcing restrictive financial conditions and credit headwinds. They support the Committee’s cautious tone and “better balance of risks,” with incremental disinflation progress but softer momentum in interest-sensitive sectors and household credit.
- Bottom line: Slightly positive on disinflation, neutral-to-slightly negative on growth; overall near neutral.
